name: Compact midface

card.summary: A short midface (the span from brow to upper lip) that community members treat as a marker of a harmonious, youthful facial-thirds balance, which people try to enhance with grooming, hairstyling or jaw/maxilla surgery.
card.note: Whether a short midface is attractive is disputed within the community itself.

quick.overview:
The midface is the middle third of the face, roughly from the brow line or nasion down to the base of the nose. A compact (short) midface means this section is short relative to the forehead and lower face, with eyes set close to the cheekbones and a short distance to the lip. In looksmaxxing forums it is often described as a youthful, dimorphic-looking trait and as part of a "harmonious" face.

Because the proportion comes mostly from bone and nose length, people work on its appearance through nose shape, philtrum length, hairstyle, facial hair and, in some cases, jaw surgery. Community views differ sharply: some call a compact midface ideal, others call it a meme or say excessively short midfaces look cramped.
quick.how: Practitioners discuss it as a ratio to assess in photos (midface versus the other facial thirds), then adjust perceived proportions with haircuts that change the forehead and upper-face balance, with facial hair, and with nose or lip-length considerations. Surgical talk centres on maxillary (Le Fort I) and jaw procedures, which change vertical proportions and are planned by a surgeon.
quick.risks: The concept is a community framework, not a clinical diagnosis. A short midface can also occur in some genetic conditions, and jaw surgery carries the usual operative risks such as swelling, infection and numbness. Over-shortening is a concern some members raise themselves.

lead: A compact midface, also called a short midface, describes a face in which the middle third (from the brow region to the base of the nose, with some members also counting the philtrum, the groove between nose and upper lip) is short in proportion to the forehead and lower face. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as part of facial harmony and is often paired with other traits such as wide cheekbones and a horizontal occlusal plane.[1][3][16]

People use the idea to evaluate their own faces in photos and to decide what to change. Because a face looks more or less compact depending on how the nose, philtrum, hairline and lower face relate to one another, the practical routes members discuss are haircuts and grooming that rebalance the upper and middle face, attention to nose and lip length, and, for a small number, consultation with an orthognathic surgeon about maxillary position.[2][4][8][12][14]

The label itself is a community framework. Academic work on facial attractiveness has examined related spacing ratios, most prominently a 2010 study that found the eye-to-mouth distance judged most attractive was about 36 percent of face length in the female faces tested, and clinical literature describes a short midface in surgical and genetic contexts.[5][6][10]

chain: Judge midface length against the other facial thirds
Adjust hair, facial hair and nose/lip balance, or consult a surgeon about maxillary position
angle.text: People use the compact midface idea as a proportion target when choosing haircuts, grooming and, for a small number, orthognathic planning. The effect on perceived attractiveness is a matter of debate in the communities that use the term.

paras: The face is commonly divided into thirds: the upper third from hairline to brow, the midface from brow to the base of the nose (or to the upper lip in some schemes), and the lower third from nose or lip to chin. A compact midface is one where the middle span is short relative to the others, giving a smaller distance between the eyes and the mouth and eyes that sit close to the cheekbones and upper lip.[1][2]

Forum users disagree on what to measure. Some say nose length and philtrum length decide how compact the midface appears, while others argue the philtrum matters little if the nose is already short.[2] A user argument on looksmax.org holds that perceived compactness is largely a function of the nose, giving examples of public figures with small noses whose faces look compact despite a long philtrum.[2]

Members also tie the term to other proportion vocabulary, including a horizontal occlusal plane, wide cheekbones and a wide skull, and use threads titled around harmony and how a short midface looks in photos to compare examples.[3][16][18]

sections.h: The philtrum and nose in midface appearance
paras: The philtrum is the vertical groove in the centre of the upper lip, running from the base of the nasal septum to the lip tubercle; it forms in the embryo where the nasomedial and maxillary processes meet.[13] Its length is one of the variables forum members point to when judging whether a midface looks short. Clinically, a flattened philtrum is described as a feature of fetal alcohol syndrome and Prader-Willi syndrome, and a shorter-than-average philtrum has been reported as part of a cluster of facial features in one study of boys with autism spectrum disorders.[13]

Surgeons shorten a long philtrum with a lip lift, in which skin is removed under the nose (subnasal or indirect lift) or along the lip border (direct lift) to raise the upper lip. A 2014 systematic review cited by Wikipedia found philtrum length decreased with indirect lip lift techniques. Complications listed include scarring, numbness, lip distortion and asymmetry.[14]

No published study has tested a compact midface as such. Related work on proportions comes from psychophysics. In a 2010 Vision Research paper, Pamela Pallett, Stephen Link and Kang Lee edited photographs of young white women's faces so that only the eye-to-mouth distance or the distance between the eyes changed, then asked students to choose the more attractive of each pair across four experiments totalling 126 participants. Attractiveness peaked when the eye-to-mouth distance was about 36 percent of face length and the interocular distance about 46 percent of face width, values the authors found to match the average face.[10][11]

The authors noted that only Caucasian female faces were tested and that male faces, other groups and children's faces remain to be studied; they proposed either an evolutionary account (selection for healthy mates favouring typical proportions) or a cognitive account (people form prototypes and find them easier to process).[10] Wikipedia's article on facial symmetry notes separately that experiments suggest symmetry and averageness make independent contributions to attractiveness.[15]
In a news interview, Pallett said hairstyles such as pulling hair back or wearing bangs can change how facial proportions appear, a point that parallels the haircut questions raised on forums.[11][4]

Threads on looksmax.org show opposing positions. Some members say they find short midfaces attractive and that their personal preference moved toward them.[1] Others call "compact midface" a meme and argue a short midface is not an ideal for men, with some defining a positive version as a well-oriented occlusal plane combined with strong cheekbones.[3] A further thread argues that a tall skull and long face are dimorphic traits, so a short midface is the less dimorphic option.[7]
Other threads ask the reverse question of how to address an "overly compact" midface, indicating that members who have the trait also discuss it as a concern rather than an asset.[17]

The disagreement is partly about definitions: a short midface, a compact midface and an overly short midface are used for different things, and members point to different measurements (nasion to subnasale, eye to lip, or ratios of the facial thirds).

Members ask which haircuts create the illusion of a more compact midface, usually by changing how much forehead is visible and how the upper and middle face are balanced,[4] and whether jaw surgery can offset a midface that is already too short.[8] These are discussion topics rather than established protocols.

Grooming-based approaches discussed in general terms include hairline and fringe styling, facial hair, and eyebrow shaping, all of which change where the eye and the eye-to-lip span appear to sit. Because the underlying proportion mostly reflects bone and nose length, surgical conversations centre on the nose, lip lift, and maxillary or jaw procedures planned by a surgeon.[14][5]

sections.h: Surgical context: Le Fort I and orthognathic surgery
paras: Orthognathic (jaw) surgery repositions the upper and lower jaws; Wikipedia notes maxillary and mandibular osteotomies date to the 1940s and that total maxillary osteotomy treats vertical maxillary excess, or long face syndrome.[12] General risks listed include bleeding, swelling, infection and facial numbness, which usually recovers within about three months.[12]

In clinical practice, a short midface in a patient with jaw deformity has been treated with a high Le Fort I osteotomy, a variant that sets the maxillary cut higher to address cheek depression. A 2020 case report describes a 17-year-old woman with facial asymmetry, mandibular protrusion, a short midface and long tooth roots, treated with a 3D-printed guide and piezosurgery to protect the roots and infraorbital nerve.[5]

The term spread through looksmax.org threads on facial thirds, harmony and dimorphism, where it is both promoted and ridiculed. Titles range from posts celebrating examples to threads asking how to fix an overly compact midface, to threads arguing the idea is a meme.[3][16][17]
Participants frequently cite photographs of public figures as examples. This article does not reproduce those judgements, which vary between threads and are opinion.

No studies found on compact midface as an attractiveness trait. The nearest research concerns facial ratios in general: the 2010 Pallett, Link and Lee experiments on eye-to-mouth and interocular spacing in female faces,[10] and surgical case reports such as the 2020 high Le Fort I description.[5]

Related medical literature describes short midface as a feature of some conditions: a 1992 case report of a mother and child with delayed cranial ossification noted a short midface among their facial features,[6] and a 2020 mouse study of osteogenesis imperfecta found a relatively short midface after scaling for body size.[9]

timeline.event: Simon Hullihen publishes an early jaw-surgery case, cited by Wikipedia as one of the first orthognathic reports.[12]
Maxillary and mandibular osteotomies are developed, according to Wikipedia's orthognathic surgery article.[12]
A case report in the American Journal of Medical Genetics describes a short midface in a mother and child with delayed cranial ossification.[6]
Pallett, Link and Lee publish 'New golden ratios for facial beauty' in Vision Research, reporting preferred eye-to-mouth and interocular ratios.[10]
A case report describes a 3D-guided high Le Fort I osteotomy in a patient with a short midface.[5]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, "compact midface" is argued over as an ideal, a meme and a fetish, and members ask how to change how their midface reads or whether it is too short.[1][3][17]

claims.claim: A compact midface is attractive and looks youthful.
claims.believers: Proponents say short midfaces read as harmonious and mention a personal shift in preference toward them.[1]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested compact midface as an attractiveness trait.

claims.claim: Compactness is mostly about the nose, not the philtrum.
claims.believers: Some users argue a short nose makes the midface look compact even with a long philtrum; others say philtrum length contributes too.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this perceptual claim.

claims.claim: Haircuts can create the illusion of a more compact midface.
claims.believers: Members ask for and swap haircut ideas aimed at rebalancing the upper and middle face.[4]
claims.experts: No studies have tested hairstyles for this effect.

claims.claim: Jaw surgery can offset a too-short midface.
claims.believers: Users ask whether orthognathic surgery changes midface proportion.[8]
claims.experts: Case reports describe Le Fort I variants planned for a short midface in jaw-deformity patients.[5]

claims.claim: Eye-to-mouth proportion has an attractive range, so facial thirds can be optimised.
claims.believers: Members who use facial-thirds analysis treat the midface as one of the measurable ratios of a harmonious face.[16]
claims.experts: A 2010 experiment found female faces were rated most attractive when the eye-to-mouth distance was about 36 percent of face length; only Caucasian female faces were tested.[10]

claims.claim: A short midface is a dimorphic ideal in men.
claims.believers: Supporters describe it as a youthful, dimorphic trait; opponents say a tall skull and long face are the dimorphic traits and a short midface is "cope".[3][7]
claims.experts: No published study has tested midface length as a sexually dimorphic attractiveness trait; the ratio study examined female faces only.[10]

claims.claim: A lip lift can make a face read as more balanced by shortening the philtrum.
claims.believers: Members who discuss philtrum length treat it as a contributor to midface length.[2]
claims.experts: A 2014 systematic review cited by Wikipedia reported philtrum length decreased after indirect lip lift techniques; scarring and lip distortion are listed complications.[14]
